I have a fully insubstantial story for you about a tiny walkman.
When I was first getting into my electronics career in the early 00s, I met a lot of old heads that were engineers or inventers when they were younger, that fell back to repair when their fields became outdated. They were all brilliant and worked on wild stuff. One of there men werr super into audio equipment.
I forget his name, but he was proud of what he made. He used to talk about making custom DSPs for rich folks' home theaters and cars 'back when dolby was o ly in theaters", and brought an old custom car magazine to show me that he allegedly pioneered the optical twinkling starscape headliner back in the early 90s or late 80s.
Well, one day he brought in a little cardboard box, and he opened it for me. Inside was the absolutely tiny little walkman thing. I say thing because it was a one way tape mech, completely cut down to the barest of parts, that strapped across the bottom of a tape with a single take up reel. The teeny little drive motor was next to the capstans and was super narrow and as long as the tape was wide, the belt was only shielded by a pair of small brass tubes with slots cut in them, and it had a pair of skinny batteries on the integrated headphone cable, next to the single play/stop button, that applied power to the whole mechanism.
And it worked! And it was completely impractical! The biggest part was where the head and tension wheel were.
Also I distinctly remember it being held together with solder and JB weld, and it had a single really sharp spot where he cut a part off and never broke the edge with a file.
